![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14194111/assets/1d1712fb97a1a508a5603e055218a863eb314310a8af74cf6344a3cd7ab50731.png)

The graph of a function $y=f(x)$ is given above. Find $a$ and $b$ such that $f(x)\to a$ as $x\to \infty $ and $f(x)\to b$ as $x\to -\infty .$
question.worked_solution:
- On the right of the graph, we see that as $x$ gets larger and larger, the function $f(x)$ levels off to the value of $0.$ We can express this as follows:

$$
f(x)\to 0\,\text{as}\,x\to \infty 
$$

Therefore, $a=0.$

- On the left of the graph, we see that as $x$ gets more and more negative, the function $f(x)$ becomes more and more negative without bound. We can express this as follows:

$$
f(x)\to -\infty \,\text{as}\,x\to -\infty 
$$

Therefore, $b=-\infty .$
